There is a low stroke between לִשְׁלִיחַ and צִבּוּר. I read it as the patach under ח, but it could be a maqaf.

blocks.text: לאמרה בכונה וברתת ובחרדה קודם התפלה.
uncertainties: Set in small rabbinic (Rashi-style) type, unpointed.

blocks.text: אֵל מֶלֶךְ נֶאֱמָן שַׁדַּי מֶלֶךְ עֶלְיוֹן קַבֵּל שַׁוְעָתִי בְּרָצוֹן וּבְאִמּוּץ הַלֵּב. יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ יְיָ אֶחָד אֵל חַי דַּיָּן אֱמֶת שׁוֹפֵט צֶדֶק רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן. רַחֵם עָלַי וּשְׁמַע תְּפִלָּתִי הַיּוֹם אֲשֶׁר אֶתְפַּלֵּל בַּעֲדִי וּבְעַד בֵּיתִי וּבְעַד עֲדָתִי הַמַּסְכִּימִים עִמִּי כִּתְפִלָּתִי וְתִכְלוֹל תְּפִלָּתִי עִם הַתְּפִלּוֹת הַיְשָׁרוֹת וְהַנְּקִיּוֹת אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשׂוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל. וְתַחְתּוֹר תַּחַת כִּסֵּא כְבוֹדֶךָ כְּמוֹ שֶׁחָתַרְתָּ לִתְפִלַּת מֹשֶׁה (כ״א מְנַשֶּׁה). וְאַל יֵבוֹשׁוּ בִי שׁוֹלְחַי וְלֹא אֲנִי בָהֶם: יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי פִי וְהֶגְיוֹן לִבִּי לְפָנֶיךָ יְיָ צוּרִי וְגוֹאֲלִי. אָמֵן סֶלָה: יְהִי רָצוֹן לְפָנֶיךָ אָיוֹם שֶׁתִּתֶּן לִי קוֹל נָעִים וְעָרֵב הַיּוֹם וְאַל יִפְסוֹק קוֹלִי וְאַל יִחַר גְּרוֹנִי וְיִהְיֶה קוֹלִי נָעִים וְחָזָק כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיְהִי קוֹל הַשּׁוֹפָר הוֹלֵךְ וְחָזֵק: אָמֵן סֶלָה:
uncertainties: The divine name is printed as two yods with pointing beneath (יְיָ). The exact placement of the points is approximated.

The parenthetical (כ״א מְנַשֶּׁה) has its abbreviation in small Rashi-style type. I read it as כ״א, meaning an alternative reading 'Menasseh', which matches the English '(Menasseh)'. It is a text variant, not a Shabbat addition or a rite direction.
Small strokes before יַעֲשׂוּ, יֵבוֹשׁוּ and וַיְהִי may be meteg/ga'ya marks or patach and are not certain.
It is unclear whether כְבוֹדֶךָ and כְדַי (in the next prayer) carry a dagesh in the kaf. I recorded them without one.
Psalms 19:15 (יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן…) and Exodus 19:19 (וַיְהִי קוֹל הַשּׁוֹפָר הוֹלֵךְ וְחָזֵק) are embedded in this prayer with no separate citation printed.

blocks.text: תפלה אחרת לש״ץ.
uncertainties: Small rabbinic type.

blocks.text: הִנְנִי הֶעָנִי מִמַּעַשׂ וְנִרְעָשׁ וְנִפְחָד מִפַּחַד יוֹשֵׁב תְּהִלּוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּאתִי לַעֲמוֹד וּלְחַנֵּן לְפָנֶיךָ עַל עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר שְׁלָחוּנִי וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינִי כְדַי וְהָגוּן לְכָךְ: עַל כֵּן אֲבַקֶּשְׁךָ אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם אֱלֹהֵי יִצְחָק וֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב. יְיָ יְיָ. אֵל רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן. אֱלֹהִים. שַׁדַּי אָיוֹם וְנוֹרָא. הֱיֵה נָא מַצְלִיחַ דַּרְכִּי אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי הוֹלֵךְ לַעֲמוֹד לְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עָלַי וְעַל שׁוֹלְחַי. וְנָא אַל תַּפְשִׁיעֵם בְּחַטֹּאתַי וְאַל תְּחַיְּבֵם בַּעֲוֹנוֹתַי כִּי חוֹטֵא וּפוֹשֵׁעַ אָנִי וְאַל יִכָּלְמוּ בִּי בִּפְשָׁעַי וְאַל יֵבוֹשׁוּ בִי וְאַל אֵבוֹשָׁה בָהֶם וְקַבֵּל תְּפִלָּתִי כִּתְפִלַּת זָקֵן וְרָגִיל וּפִרְקוֹ נָאֶה וּזְקָנוֹ מְגֻדָּל וְקוֹלוֹ נָעִים וּמְעֹרָב בְּדַעַת עִם הַבְּרִיּוֹת. וְתִגְעַר בְּשָׂטָן לְבַל יַשְׂטִינֵנוּ. וִיהִי נָא דִגְלֵנוּ עָלֶיךָ אַהֲבָה. לְכָל פְּשָׁעִים תְּכַסֶּה בְּאַהֲבָה. וְכָל צוֹמוֹתֵינוּ וְעִנּוּיֵינוּ הֲפֹךְ לָנוּ וּלְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְשָׂשׂוֹן וּלְשִׂמְחָה לְחַיִּים וּלְשָׁלוֹם. הָאֱמֶת וְהַשָּׁלוֹם אֱהָבוּ וְאַל יְהִי שׁוּם מִכְשׁוֹל בִּתְפִלָּתִי:
uncertainties: The image shows אֲבַקֶּשְׁךָ, ending in final kaf with qamats, not the more common אֲבַקֵּשׁ.
At this scan resolution, dagesh in כְדַי, דִגְלֵנוּ and בִי is uncertain.
The pointing of וּמְעֹרָב (holam) and מְגֻדָּל (qubbutz) is read from the image but is small.

blocks.text: וִיהִי רָצוֹן לְפָנֶיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם אֱלֹהֵי יִצְחָק וֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב הָאֵל הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא אֵל עֶלְיוֹן אֶהְיֶה אֲשֶׁר אֶהְיֶה שֶׁכָּל הַמַּלְאָכִים שֶׁהֵם בַּעֲלֵי תְפִלּוֹת יָבִיאוּ תְּפִלָּתִי לִפְנֵי כִסֵּא כְבוֹדֶךָ וְיָפִיצוּ אוֹתָהּ לְפָנֶיךָ בַּעֲבוּר כָּל הַצַּדִּיקִים וְהַחֲסִידִים הַתְּמִימִים וְהַיְשָׁרִים וּבַעֲבוּר כְּבוֹד שִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא כִּי אַתָּה שׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִלַּת עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּרַחֲמִים בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה שׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִלָּה:
uncertainties: The three occurrences of אֱלֹהֵי / וֵאלֹהֵי are printed with the alef-lamed ligature (ﭏ). They are written out here as full letters.
The divine name יְיָ runs into the following word in print with no clear space.

blocks.text: קבלה מרי״ם לומר ד׳ פסוקים אלו, קודם שמתחיל הש״ץ המלך וקודם הקדיש:
uncertainties: The abbreviation after קבלה reads as מרי״ם, but it is small Rashi-style type and could be another abbreviation, such as מהרי״ם. Its expansion is not certain.
Unpointed rabbinic type.

blocks.text: A Prayer for the Reader
אל

O God, faithful King, Almighty, Supreme King, accept my devoted and confident prayer. O Lord our God, the Lone God, the living God, the truthful judge, the righteous ruler, merciful and gracious, have mercy upon me and hear my prayer today when I pray for myself and my family and all my congregation who join in my prayers. Include my prayer among the upright and pure prayers that Israel offers, and let it come beneath Thy glorious throne just as Thou didst to the prayer of Moses (Menasseh), so that those who sent me may not be put to shame through me, nor I through them. May the words of my mouth find favour and the meditation of my heart before Thee, O Lord, my Rock and my Redeemer, Amen, Selah. May it be Thy will, O Awe-inspiring One, to give me a pleasant and sweet voice today so that my voice may not fail me and my throat not burn; let my voice be pleasant and strong, as it is written: ‘And the sound of the Shofar increased in strength’. Amen, Selah.
uncertainties: The source hyphenates 'gra-cious' across a line break. Here it is joined.

blocks.text: הנני

Behold I come, poor in deeds, shaking and trembling with fear, before Him, who is enthroned above Israel’s songs of praise, to appear and entreat before Thee for Thy people Israel, who have sent me, although I am neither deserving nor worthy of this. Therefore I implore Thee, God of Abraham, God of Isaac and God of Jacob, O Lord, Lord, merciful and gracious God, O God, Almighty, fearful and awe-inspiring, let my way meet with success, for I am about to approach to beg mercy for myself and those who send me. Hold them not guilty for my sins, do not condemn them because of my guilt, for I am a sinner and transgressor; may they not be put to shame because of my transgressions, let them not be disgraced through me nor I through them. Accept my prayer as if it were the prayer of an elder, who is experienced, whose conduct is seemly, whose beard is imposing, whose voice is pleasant and who enjoys the love of his fellow men. Rebuke Satan that he may not oppose us. Let our banner before Thee be love, cover all transgressions with love, transform our fasts and our afflictions for us and all Israel into joy and mirth, for life and peace. Love truth and peace; and let there be no hindrance in my prayer.
uncertainties: The source hyphenates 'im-plore' and 'ap-proach' across line breaks. Here they are joined.

blocks.text: ויהי

May it be Thy will, O Lord, God of Abraham, God of Isaac and God of Jacob, great, strong and awe-inspiring God, supreme God, whose name is: “I am that I am”, that all the angels who are bearers of prayers, may bring my prayer before Thy glorious throne and spread it before Thee, for the sake of all the righteous, the pious, the perfect and the upright and for the sake of Thy great, strong and awe-inspiring Name; for Thou hearest the prayer of Thy people Israel in compassion. Blessed art Thou, hearer of prayer.
ידעתי
I know, O Lord, that Thy judgments are justice, and faithfully hast Thou chastised me.
uncertainties: The source hyphenates 'faith-fully' across a line break, with a hanging indent. Here it is joined.

blocks.text: Listen to me and answer me when I lament and sigh.
Let my soul exult in the Lord, rejoice in His help.
It is He who gives salvation to kings, who saves His servant David from the evil sword.
uncertainties: 'from the evil sword' sits on a second line with a hanging indent.

notes: Both scans carry printed page number 89 in both upper corners. s198 is the Hebrew page and s199 is the English facing page.
The Hebrew page has no English text at the bottom, and the English page has no footnotes. Below the last English verse there is only a short centred horizontal rule. Nothing appears after it.
Neither page has any Shabbat additions, sound (shofar) sequences, or German instructions in Hebrew script. The only parenthetical is (כ״א מְנַשֶּׁה) / (Menasseh), which is a text variant.

No printed biblical citations appear on either page. I supplied the Psalms references for the four closing verses myself. Embedded quotations (Psalms 19:15 and Exodus 19:19) are noted inside the first prayer's uncertainties.
The Hebrew is fully pointed but has no cantillation that I can see, including in the four Psalms verses. A few marks that look like meteg cannot be confirmed at this resolution.
The rubrics are in small rabbinic type. Abbreviations are kept as printed, without expanding them.
The enlarged bands overlap. Overlapping lines were transcribed once.
